S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in responsibilities at work (e.g., promotion, demotion)
patient_info.stressor: Maria was asked midyear to coordinate her school’s new bilingual social-emotional learning rollout while still teaching full time, mentoring novice teachers, and maintaining family and community commitments. She initially saw the role as a natural extension of her values, weaving Puerto Rican music, art, and bilingual texts into training materials, but across 5 months her stress-related reactions increasingly disrupted lesson planning, salsa nights, watercolor time, and her usual confidence in the classroom. The impairment remained limited but clear: colleagues noticed she was less consistent with deadlines and she found herself avoiding tasks she would normally handle with ease. Wanting to address the problem before it affected her students further, Maria contacted the district employee assistance program and was referred for psychiatric evaluation.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: I came in because ever since the district put this bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on my plate on top of my regular teaching, I still get through the day, but I feel wound up and discouraged in a way that isn't like me, and I've started putting off lesson plans and emails I used to handle without a second thought.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: Symptoms must develop within 3 months of the onset of the stressor
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: I started feeling unlike myself within the first month or two after they added the bilingual SEL rollout to my full teaching load; before that change, I was managing my usual work and commitments pretty well.

additional_requirement_2.name: Additional Requirement 2
additional_requirement_2.description: Within 6 months of the termination of the stressor or its consequences
additional_requirement_2.manifestation: The rollout responsibilities are still ongoing, so this has not been something that continued long after the situation ended.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I am still teaching and meeting my basic responsibilities, but I have missed or pushed back planning deadlines and needed reminders from colleagues for tasks I used to complete reliably.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about five months, since the district assigned me the rollout role midyear.
